title: The Lesson I Learned When Saul Built a Monument for Himself
paragraphs:
The Lesson I Learned When Saul Built a Monument for Himself
(1 Samuel 15:12)
He won a battle.
Then built a monument to himself.
That detail should terrify every person who says they want to be used by God.

In 1 Samuel 15:12, Saul had just come from a moment where he should have been broken, grateful, trembling before the Lord. Instead, he set up a marker for his own name. Not God’s glory. Not God’s mercy. His own image.
And that is the lesson that cut me deep:
You can look successful in public while rotting in private pride.

Saul still had the title.
Still had the crown.
Still had the language of obedience.
But his heart had already started drifting from worship to self-preservation.
That is the danger.

Not only open rebellion.
But subtle self-exaltation.
The kind that says, “Yes, Lord,” with the lips while secretly building a platform for self.
Saul’s monument was not just made of stone.

It was made of ego.
Of half-obedience.
Of wanting credit for what only God could have done.
And here is where the warning becomes personal:
Every time I want applause more than holiness, I am laying bricks for my own monument.
Every time I obey only the parts of God’s Word that are convenient, I am thinking like Saul.
Every time I protect my reputation more than I protect my surrender, I am walking near a cliff.
But here’s what we miss:

The story is not only about Saul’s failure.
It is also about our need for a better King.

Saul built monuments for himself.
Jesus made Himself of no reputation.

Saul clung to honor.
Jesus humbled Himself, even to the point of death on a cross.

Saul used leadership to preserve self.
Jesus used His authority to save sinners.

That is why the answer to pride is not merely “try harder.”
It is repent and look to Christ.

Because pride cannot be healed by self-improvement.
It must be crucified.
And only Jesus can do that in us.
So the lesson I learned from Saul’s monument is this:
The moment I start stealing glory, I am already losing the one thing that matters most — a heart fully yielded to God.

Lord, tear down every monument in me.
Every hidden altar to ego.
Every craving for credit.
Every polished version of disobedience.
And build in me a heart that trembles at Your Word.

There is hope for people like us.
Not in our record.
Not in our image.
But in the mercy of Jesus Christ.

He still rescues the proud who repent.
He still restores the broken who bow.
He still tears down idols and makes sons out of rebels.

“To obey is better than sacrifice…”
— 1 Samuel 15:22
